title: Theory x CLO
transcript:
Fabric fit and timeless style—that hasn't changed since the day we opened our doors. We've always looked at what's new, what's next, incorporating fabric and timeless style into our innovation. A number of years ago, I saw 3D; I literally called Andrew and said, "Andrew, we have to have this. This would save a lot of time and a lot of effort." We have now done this for two different retailers who will have ideas; we'll do it all in 3D and we'll see what it looks like before we even make sample one, and we'll show it to the retailers that way. So we're actually saving a lot of time and a lot of money, and eventually, I think it's going to enhance our creativity because we'll be able to do things even faster.

When we first started looking at 3D software, what CLO offered us was that their focus is on the front end—the creative process—and that really matched what our business is looking for in a 3D tool. You're able to look at something that's much more meaningful than a sketch or a line sheet; you're able to see what the actual product looks like without having to manufacture an actual sample. Certain categories that may have been challenging with other software, we were able to create our full line using CLO, which is much more user-friendly for designers and merchandisers. That business partnership is very key in having that buy-in and really engaging our designers and merchandisers in the use of the tool.

Our vision is not to look at this as a 3D project but rather this is just now the way we work. We want them to use this instead of the traditional methods of hand sketching and using tools like Adobe Illustrator. We're going to use 3D end-to-end, all the way through manufacturing of the garment, having this 3D model living with the actual specifications and samples. It just becomes part of the overall process.

The previous 3D that we were using, you couldn't design on it. CLO has taken it even further than I had originally imagined, designing things and putting the fabrics in them so that the fabrics can drape properly, and determining, "Oh, you know, I really want that fabric," or, "You know what, that fabric's not really right," without even wanting a sample yardage. I mean, there are so many opportunities for the future. It's really exciting.

chunks.title: Theory x CLO
chunks.content: ## Introduction to 3D Technology in Apparel Design This section explains the integration of 3D technology, specifically CLO software, in apparel design and manufacturing, highlighting its impact on creativity, efficiency, and business processes. Fabric fit and timeless style have always been central to the brand's identity. The adoption of 3D technology marks a significant innovation, enabling the company to visualize garments digitally before producing physical samples. This approach saves considerable time and money by allowing designers and retailers to review and adjust designs virtually, reducing the need for multiple physical prototypes. The company has successfully applied 3D processes for two different retailers, conducting the entire design evaluation digitally. This shift not only streamlines traditional workflows but is anticipated to enhance creative capabilities by accelerating design iterations. ## Advantages of CLO Software for Design and Merchandising This section details the specific benefits of CLO software, emphasizing its user-friendly interface for designers and merchandisers and its focus on the creative process in 3D garment visualization. Unlike previous 3D tools, CLO centers on the front end of design, matching the company's requirement for a tool that supports creativity over mere visualization. CLO enables viewing of realistic 3D garments that look much more meaningful than sketches or line sheets, allowing stakeholders to evaluate products without manufacturing physical samples. The software supports the creation of full product lines, including challenging categories, with greater ease. Its user-friendly interface encourages adoption by designers and merchandisers, fostering business-wide engagement and buy-in. This partnership between the company and CLO is critical in integrating the tool into daily workflows. ## Vision for End-to-End 3D Workflow in Garment Production This section outlines the company's strategic vision to fully integrate 3D technology into every stage of garment design and manufacturing, replacing traditional methods like hand sketching and Adobe Illustrator. The goal is to make 3D the standard working method rather than a separate project. Designers will use CLO software from initial design through to manufacturing, maintaining a living 3D model that includes all specifications and sample data. This digital integration aims to streamline communication and reduce errors throughout the production pipeline. By embedding 3D models into the core process, the company anticipates improved accuracy and efficiency, ultimately transforming its operational workflow. ## Enhanced Fabric Simulation and Future Opportunities with CLO This section focuses on CLO's advanced fabric simulation capabilities and the potential for future innovation in fabric selection and garment design. Previous 3D solutions lacked robust design capabilities, but CLO surpasses these limitations by allowing designers to apply fabrics that drape realistically on virtual garments. This enables designers to make informed choices about fabric suitability without needing physical yardage samples. Such accurate simulation opens numerous possibilities, from faster design decisions to experimenting with fabric behavior virtually. The company views these advancements as exciting opportunities that will continue to evolve, further enhancing creativity and reducing resource consumption in the design process.
